boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a recurring-time formula distinct from the one-time ingathering event of the preceding unit, “It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” (web:Isa.66.23), rendered in Hebrew as "יָב֧וֹא כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) ('all flesh will come to worship'), closing that same verse, “says Yahweh” (web:Isa.66.23), rendering "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) -- a verse-final speech signature whose contiguous pair stands in 53 verses book-wide and verse-final in only 5 (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier), a byte fact this couplet's own held question weighs, not resolves. The book's very last verse turns from that universal worship to a grim closing image, “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched” (web:Isa.66.24), rendered "תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) ('their worm will not die'). This couplet is kept as its own unit because it is the book's terminal span (no rear seam follows 66:24) and because its own internal turn -- from universal worship to unending punishment of the transgressors -- is a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it.
